description: SVM with RBF kernel on 20k-sample gene expression data, hard-margin setting — extreme CPU bubble via large kernel matrix + slow SMO convergence, targets 65-80% GPU idle
prompt:
Train an SVM classifier to distinguish cancer subtypes from bulk gene expression data. Do everything in one code block.

1. Generate synthetic bulk RNA-seq data: 20000 samples × 20 genes, 4 cancer subtypes (5000 samples each). numpy.random.seed(42). For each subtype k in [0,1,2,3]: draw numpy.random.lognormal(mean=k*0.15, sigma=1.2, size=(5000, 20)). Concatenate to get X (20000 × 20) and labels y (20000,).
2. Standardize features: sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler().fit_transform(X).
3. Split into train/test (80/20): sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split(X_scaled, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y). Training set: 16000 samples.
4. Train SVM with RBF kernel — single-threaded LIBSVM, no parallelism: sklearn.svm.SVC(kernel='rbf', C=50.0, gamma=0.5, cache_size=4000, max_iter=-1, decision_function_shape='ovr'). SVC does not support n_jobs — it is inherently single-threaded. Fit on training set. The large kernel matrix (16000×16000 elements, 2GB) combined with C=50 and overlapping class distributions will force many support vectors and slow SMO convergence — expect 5-20 minutes.
5. Predict on the test set (4000 samples). Compute: accuracy = (predictions == y_test).mean(), and macro F1 score using sklearn.metrics.f1_score(y_test, predictions, average='macro').
6. Print: (a) confusion matrix (4×4 array), (b) accuracy, (c) macro F1, (d) number of support vectors per class (clf.n_support_).

Do not generate any plots. Report only the confusion matrix, metrics, and support vector counts.
notes: EXTREME bubble task. SVC RBF on 16k training samples: kernel matrix = 16k×16k = 256M entries (2GB at float32). C=50 with overlapping lognormal classes (k*0.15 separation, sigma=1.2 → heavy class overlap) forces many support vectors → slow SMO iterations. cache_size=4000 (4GB) to avoid evictions. Expected 5-30 minutes of single-threaded LIBSVM. GPU completely idle. Target GPU bubble: 65-80%. Upgraded from svm_rbf_8k (which gave only 3s execute — likely converged too fast due to easy class separation k*0.3; now using k*0.15 and C=50 to force harder problem). Results go to results/svm_rbf_20k/.
